cec2a8e7a175ade89ce5588e47697f212d98e2a9.summary: A malware-analysis blog post, published 2018-08-08 and archived 2026-11-25, on recovering the configuration of JRAT/Adwind malware with the x32dbg debugger. The post says the malware first creates a fake JAR and config to confuse analysts, then starts several processes, including checks for AV products via WMI. It says the real config can be found in memory by searching for a known string. No threat actor, sector or country is named.
